clue.text: A Manx cat and dog eating very round fruit

indicators.note: the A, cat and dog letters take the next pieces into their middle, as if eating them
a Manx cat has no tail, so cat and dog both lose their last letters

parts.note: the animal word taken as written before docking
the animal word taken as written before docking
a round shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: A tailless Isle of Man cat and a dog are chewing on some very round piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' (the tailless breed from the Isle of Man) docks both animals, giving CA and DO; 'eating' puts V and O inside A + CADO.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped tropical fruit, so fruit is its general category.

clue.text: See 4
Old business journal edition lacking content repeatedly

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, Britain's business daily

indicators.note: an edition with its contents emptied out leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An old edition of the financial paper has nothing in it, time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, Britain's pink business newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means many times, frequently, which is to say repeatedly.

clue.text: Wretched existence if deals go badly

indicators.note: deals going badly means the letters go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Life is miserable when business deals go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a miserable, hard life, as dogs were once treated harshly.

clue.text: Prepare no toad-in-the-hole, and strange how unintended result arises

indicators.note: preparing a dish works the ingredients into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fail to cook the sausage-in-batter dish and, oddly, things spiral out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter. 'Prepare' rearranges its letters with NO and STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a chain of events where each step leads on, producing an outcome nobody planned.

clue.text: Female engulfed by anger in Winchester?

indicators.note: the female letter is swallowed up inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: A woman is overcome with rage somewhere in the city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester looks like the Hampshire cathedral city; the question mark flags it as a definition by example, the famous make of gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester is a celebrated make of repeating firearm, one example of a long gun.

clue.text: Larger than usual, like Henry VIII

definitions.meaning: ... is a size larger than standard, as in a ... flush or paper size
Henry VIII was a king, so kingly or regal

explanation.surface: Of a size bigger than normal, like the famously stout Tudor king.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a large paper or bed size and describes anything belonging to a monarch.

clue.text: Fire ghost mysteriously appears in vision

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and unclear, so the letters of fire ghost come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A spectral figure made of flame turns up in someone's dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision in the sense of far-sightedness, the ability to plan for what lies ahead.

clue.text: Educated English smutty about sex

indicators.note: the smutty word wraps around the sex word

parts.note: rude here means indecent, smutty
it is old slang for sex, or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A well-schooled Englishman tells dirty jokes about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means learned, having great knowledge from study.

clue.text: Field marshal in explosively gory moment

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters of gory moment are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior army commander features in a bloody, explosive moment of battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Montgomery, Monty of El Alamein, held the highest British army rank of field marshal.

clue.text: Runs away in defeat

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
out means away, as in gone out or not at home

explanation.surface: An army flees in the face of defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, disorderly defeat in battle or sport.

clue.text: At which point wife gets chicken

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken

explanation.surface: Someone asks at what moment the wife was given a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: As a relative adverb it means at the time or moment that something happens.

clue.text: Pedant thus collars companion — only one left in charge

indicators.note: the word for thus grabs the companion letters, holding them inside

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
the last one is the only one left

explanation.surface: A fussy pedant grabs a companion, so that only one person remains in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholastic is a hair-splitting academic in the medieval schoolmen's tradition, a pedant.

clue.text: Song about knave, knight and rustic

indicators.note: the song goes round, about, the knave

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a dishonourable man, a knave
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A ballad about a rogue, a knight and a country fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia was the idealised pastoral land of Greek poetry, so its adjective means pastoral, rural.

clue.text: Philosopher having noble title and renouncing it

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, a noble

indicators.note: giving something up, so the word it is dropped from title

parts.note: the word title taken as written before the cut
the word it taken as written, removed

explanation.surface: A thinker who held an aristocratic title gives it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker who tutored Alexander the Great is among the most famous philosophers.

clue.text: Score first in tournament — that's Little Bird!

parts.note: an eagle is a golf score of two under par

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of tournament

explanation.surface: A golfer scores early in a tournament, perhaps a nickname for a young player called Little Bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, literally a little bird of that kind.

clue.text: Squiffy ladette straddles doctor engaged in controversy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit astride the doctor letters, enclosing them
squiffy means tipsy, so the letters of ladette are drunkenly jumbled

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A tipsy young woman sits astride a doctor amid scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladette is a British term for a boisterous, hard-drinking young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embattled is beset by conflict or criticism, fighting on all sides.

clue.text: Miss Liddell joins Mike in desire to do harm

indicators.note: Alice is placed after the M, joining it

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Alice Liddell was the girl who inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A young girl teams up with a man called Mike out of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, the intention to hurt someone.

clue.text: Silver bullet having struck bottom

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a single bullet or shell

explanation.surface: A silver bullet has hit its target at the very base.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship aground has run onto the seabed or shore, so it has struck the bottom.

clue.text: Wine to honour hero impaling one vampire? The opposite!

indicators.note: one piece goes through the other, as a stake through a body
turns round the containment: the hero is run through by the vampire letters rather than doing the impaling

parts.note: a lion is a brave person, a hero, as in a literary lion
I is the Roman numeral for one
the vampire bat is the blood-drinking bat

explanation.surface: A wine is offered to a hero who stakes a vampire, or rather it goes the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the hero would go inside the vampire; 'The opposite!' flips the containment, so the hero's letters enclose the one-plus-vampire pair instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is wine poured out as an offering in honour of a god or the dead.

clue.text: Sinister order in America enlisting Oscar

indicators.note: taking a recruit into the ranks, so the Oscar letter is drawn inside

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
US is the United States, America
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dark order in the States signs up a man named Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means threatening, suggesting something bad will happen.

clue.text: Parents angry with tot expressing dissent

indicators.note: in a temper, so the letters of parents and tot are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad get cross with their toddler, who is objecting loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Protestant as an adjective means protesting, making a formal objection, the original sense of the church name.

clue.text: Bear to adopt upright position

explanation.surface: A bear rises onto its hind legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to put up with and to rise onto one's feet.

clue.text: Signal to stop bombardment

definitions.meaning: to ... a taxi is to wave it down to stop
a ... of bullets or stones is a heavy barrage

explanation.surface: A warning to cease firing in a barrage.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is calling out to a vehicle; the other is a shower of missiles falling thick and fast.

clue.text: Agitated male provided with accommodation perhaps

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
put up means given lodging; in a down clue PUT written upwards reads TUP, which perhaps flags

explanation.surface: A man gets worked up after being given a room for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided with accommodation' is put up; in this down entry PUT is written going up, so it reads TUP from the top, the cryptic sense 'perhaps' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is informal for worked up, excited or anxious.

clue.text: Absolutely reasonable

definitions.meaning: as in ... perfect, meaning absolutely or completely
a ... decision is fair and reasonable

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an intensifying adverb, as in just right, and as an adjective for fair, well-founded.

clue.text: Release from duty sailor with answers to crossword

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
the solution is the set of answers to a crossword

explanation.surface: A seaman is relieved of his obligations once he has filled in the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is a formal freeing from guilt or obligation, as when one is absolved of a duty.

clue.text: Awesome Rastafarian

definitions.meaning: ... as an old adjective means inspiring awe or terror, as in ... sovereign
a Rastafarian, from the dreadlocks worn

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic adjective for awe-inspiring and a slang noun for a dreadlocked Rastafarian.

clue.text: Pseudo intellectual's beginning to reform incestuous son

indicators.note: reforming means reshaping, so the letters are rearranged into a new order
the beginning of intellectual's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pretentious thinker sets out to reform a son with incestuous tendencies, a Freudian touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Oedipus unknowingly married his mother Jocasta, so he is the archetypal incestuous son.
